feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (forward row at y = 0.06, x = ±0.04, body_length 0.22, kp 2.2, kd 0.30) is the best raced result at 203.20. Oval max_error fell to 0.0598 and progress rose to 0.87, but oval steering_oscillation rose from 0.246 to 0.339, and s-bend and slalom still exit at max_error 0.0615 and 0.0611 with progress 0.17 and 0.12. Earlier iterations show that yaw inertia (body_length 0.16 to 0.20) moved oscillation only from 0.274 to 0.246, so geometry is a weak damping lever and the controller has to carry it. Outer sensors at x = ±0.04 were the bend-entry sensors in iterations 1 to 3, and line_loss_events stayed at 0.9 to 1.0 with 16 mm footprints, so there is room to move them outward. If the next race shows oval oscillation below about 0.3 and s-bend or slalom max_error still at or above 0.06 with line_loss at or below 1.0, the bend-entry problem is the outer-sensor spacing, and the next geometry step is requested change 1. If line_loss_events rise above 1.0 on any track, the outer 16 mm footprints are overlapping near the tape edge and requested change 2 applies. If oval progress falls below 0.8 while max_error stays under 0.06, the wider pair is not the cause and the next step is the controller again, not geometry.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 while line_loss_events stay at or below 1.0: try sensor_size 0.012 with the outer pair at x = ±0.05 and y = 0.06, so the footprints are smaller and the outer sensors react to the bend exit. Evidence: iterations 1 to 3 kept 16 mm footprints, and line loss stayed at 0.9 to 1.0, so the 16 mm size has not yet been tested against 12 mm at the wider spacing.

If line_loss_events rise above 1.0 per run on any track: keep sensor_size 0.016 but return the outer sensors to x = ±0.04 at y = 0.06. Evidence: iteration 3 line loss was 0.9 on the oval and 1.0 elsewhere with ±0.04, so a rise after widening would point to outer footprints leaving the tape on tight bends.

If oval progress drops below 0.8 while max_error stays under 0.06: try wheel_track 0.085 m for more turn authority, holding body_length 0.22. Evidence: moving wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 in iteration 2 raised oval progress from 0.46 to 0.53, while body_length alone changed oscillation only from 0.274 to 0.246.
